content.1_the_2026_tool_landscape:
### Comparison matrix

| Dimension | Detox | Maestro | Appium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Testing approach | Gray-box (in-process monitoring) | Black-box (accessibility layer) | Black-box (WebDriver protocol) |
| Synchronization | Native idle monitor (JS thread, UI queue, network, animations) | Implicit waits + automatic retries on UI hierarchy | Manual waits / explicit polling |
| Authoring format | JavaScript / TypeScript (`detox test`) | YAML (declarative flows) | Any WebDriver client (JS, Python, Java, etc.) |
| React Native integration | Deepest - hooks into RN bridge | Works through accessibility tree (no RN instrumentation needed) | Platform-agnostic via XCUITest/UIAutomator |
| Flakiness (production reports) | <2% | <1% | Higher; well-known flake profile |
| Login-flow execution time | ~8-12s | ~12-18s | 20s+ typical |
| Best fit | Deep RN-internal flows, native module regressions, complex async orchestration | Smoke tests, cross-platform parity, non-dev authoring, fast onboarding | Cross-platform with web parity, large existing test suites |
| CI posture | Requires custom build artifacts; "Detox Build" step | `maestro test` over any installed binary; Maestro Cloud for parallel farms | Appium server + WebDriver; needs vendor plugins |

Sources: Maestro "Detox vs. Maestro" (March 2026), reactnativecoders.com "End-to-End Testing in React Native 2026" (Feb 2026), Testsigma comparison (Nov 2025).

### Authoring trade-offs

- Detox tests are TypeScript, so they fit naturally into monorepos and CI lint/typecheck pipelines. Tests share code with the app (helpers, fixtures, mock servers), which speeds up refactors.
- Maestro flows are YAML, which lets product managers, QA, and designers author cases. A `flow.yaml` file is typically 60-80% shorter than the equivalent Detox spec for the same journey.
- Appium remains relevant when a single suite must cover web + iOS + Android or when an organisation already has a WebDriver-based infrastructure.

---
content.2_recommended_test_architecture_2026:
### The risk-based testing pyramid

1. Unit tests (~70% of cases) - Jest 30 in Node, pure functions, reducers, hooks under `renderHook`.
2. Component tests (~20%) - React Native Testing Library against `jest-react-native` preset; query by `accessibilityLabel` / `testID` and assert user-visible output.
3. E2E tests (~10%) - A small set of revenue-critical journeys: onboarding/login, primary purchase or signup, deep link, push permission, backgrounding/resume.

This ratio matches what the React Native Relay 2026 testing guide and reactnativecoders.com enterprise guide recommend. Trying to cover every screen with E2E produces a brittle, slow suite; focusing E2E on revenue/regulatory paths maximises risk reduction per second of CI time.

### Selectors that survive across layers

- For unit/component: `testID` is fine.
- For E2E: always set both `testID` (Jest) and `accessibilityIdentifier` / `accessibilityLabel` so Detox, Maestro, and Appium can all target the element deterministically.
- Avoid text-only selectors in E2E - copy changes should not break tests. Add a `data-testid`-style attribute and use that in flows.

### Mocking boundary

- MSW (Mock Service Worker) v2 at the network boundary for unit/component tests.
- For E2E, prefer a real backend on a staging environment; reserve API mocking for performance or offline-recovery tests.

---
content.3_instrumentation_and_observability:
### OpenTelemetry JS for React Native

The OpenTelemetry demo app documents the canonical setup: a `useTracer` hook in `_layout.tsx` initialises the SDK before the UI mounts, so the first user interaction is captured. Components used:

- `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-web` with `WebTracerProvider` and a `BatchSpanProcessor` wrapping an OTLP HTTP exporter.
- `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-fetch` and `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-xml-http-request` for auto-instrumenting HTTP and fetch calls.
- `@opentelemetry/core` `CompositePropagator` with `W3CBaggagePropagator` and `W3CTraceContextPropagator` for header propagation.
- `resourceFromAttributes` adds service identity (`ATTR_SERVICE_NAME = react-native-app`), OS (`ATTR_OS_NAME`, `ATTR_OS_VERSION`), and device (`ATTR_DEVICE_ID`, `ATTR_SERVICE_VERSION`) attributes.

Caveat noted in OTel docs: JS OTel packages are officially supported for Node and browser; React Native reuse works but is "not explicitly supported" - plan for occasional version pinning work.

### What to capture in an E2E test run

- Trace spans: tap events, navigation transitions, fetch calls, screen renders.
- Attributes: `test.id`, `test.suite`, `device.model`, `os.version`, `app.build`, `git.sha`.
- Logs: structured JSON via `pino` or `winston` with the same trace context.
- Metrics: cold-start time, time-to-interactive, frame drops, JS thread block time.

Wiring this through a single OTLP collector (Grafana Tempo, Honeycomb, Datadog) lets a CI failure be correlated with the trace that produced it.

### Real-device observability (production)

For production telemetry beyond tests, Embrace (open-source SDK) provides React Native instrumentation that emits session-level observability, including cold-start, network, and crash data. It complements OTel by adding user-centric metrics not available from raw traces.

---
content.4_ci_cd_patterns_that_work:
### Pipeline shape (typical enterprise setup)

1. PR open -> lint + typecheck + unit + component tests (under 5 min).
2. Merge to main -> E2E on real devices in parallel (smoke set, ~15 min).
3. Nightly -> full E2E matrix (region x device x OS) with rerun on flake.
4. Release candidate -> E2E on physical device farm (BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, Maestro Cloud).

### Tooling

- Bitrise (commercial) now defaults to M4 Pro / high-spec AMD Linux runners, with built-in flaky-test auto-quarantine and remote "live machine" sessions for debugging.
- GitHub Actions remains common; cache the JS bundle, use `expo prebuild` artifacts, and matrix on iOS simulator and Android emulator.
- Maestro Cloud runs parallel flows over real devices with HTML reports and trace replay.

### Determinism rules

- Disable animations in CI (`device.disableSynchronization()` in Detox; `--debug` or `accessibility` flags in Maestro).
- Stub push notifications and deep links with deterministic payloads.
- Use `await waitFor(... condition ...)` patterns; never `sleep`/`waitForTimeout` longer than needed.
- Seed any state via API calls before the flow runs (avoid typing through onboarding).
- Run iOS and Android against the same logical flow file (or test ID set) to catch parity regressions early.

---
content.5_best_practice_checklist:
**Strategy**

- [ ] Adopt the risk-based pyramid (70/20/10); reserve E2E for revenue-critical paths.
- [ ] Choose tools by team profile: Detox for RN-heavy teams, Maestro for cross-functional authoring, Appium only when parity with web matters.
- [ ] Maintain a single selector strategy: `testID` + `accessibilityIdentifier` on every interactive element.

**Test design**

- [ ] Author each E2E flow as a small, independent script with setup/teardown.
- [ ] Treat test data as code: factories and seeded backend state, not UI-driven setup.
- [ ] Cap E2E wall-clock at 15 minutes per PR; longer sets run nightly.

**Instrumentation**

- [ ] Initialise OTel before the root component mounts via a `useTracer` hook.
- [ ] Tag spans with `test.id`, `device.model`, `os.version`, `app.build`, `git.sha`.
- [ ] Propagate W3C `traceparent` so E2E traces correlate with backend traces.
- [ ] Adopt Embrace or similar for production crash and session observability.

**CI/CD**

- [ ] Run unit + component on every PR; gate merges on green.
- [ ] Run a smoke E2E matrix on merge to main; full matrix nightly.
- [ ] Quarantine flaky tests for auto-rerun; review quarantine weekly.
- [ ] Cache builds, share simulator state, parallelise across at least 4 devices.

**Reporting and signal**

- [ ] Attach screenshots, screen recordings, and trace IDs to every failure.
- [ ] Track flake rate as a first-class metric (target <2% for Detox, <1% for Maestro).
- [ ] Diff coverage and trace metrics between releases to catch regressions before users do.

---
content.6_common_pitfalls_and_how_to_avoid_them:
- Over-reliance on E2E. If unit and component coverage is thin, E2E cannot compensate; invest in Jest/RNTL first.
- Brittle text selectors. Localise strings or use accessibility IDs.
- Skipping the New Architecture (Fabric/TurboModules). Tests that bypass it miss the dominant runtime; ensure E2E runs against the New Architecture build.
- Ignoring flakes. Auto-quarantine alone hides problems; couple with weekly triage and a flake budget.
- Production-only observability. Without traces from E2E, failures lack the context needed to debug in production.

---
content.7_bottom_line:
For most React Native teams in July 2026, the pragmatic stack is:

- Jest 30 + React Native Testing Library for unit/component.
- Maestro for cross-platform E2E authoring (with Detox retained for RN-internal flows where gray-box sync matters).
- OpenTelemetry JS for instrumentation, exporting via OTLP HTTP to a unified backend.
- Bitrise or GitHub Actions with a four-way device matrix and auto-quarantine.
- Embrace (or equivalent) for production observability that bridges test and production traces.

This combination delivers fast feedback, deterministic E2E, and end-to-end visibility from a tap in CI to a production crash report.
